key: We have accepted thousands from Dhvasra’s and Purusanti’s hands: Swift runs this giver of delight.
s: Closing a hymn to Soma, the singers turn to the gifts received; Sāyaṇa, on 9.58.3, takes the givers as kings and cites the Śāṭyāyanaka, where two seers, feeling like swallowers of poison, saw this hymn and by it made their gain as if unaccepted.

evidence.words: ध्वस्रः कश्चिद्राजा पुरुषन्तिः कश्चित् । तयोरुभयोः । अत्र इतरेतरयोगविवक्षया द्विवचनं द्रष्टव्यम् । “सहस्राणि धनानां सहस्राणि “आ “दद्महे वयं प्रतिगृह्णीमः । तदस्माभिः प्रतिगृहीतं धनमुत्तममस्त्विति ऋषिः सोमं प्रार्थयत इति सोमस्य स्तुतिः । सिद्धमन्यत् । यथावत्सार एतयोर्धनानि प्रतिजग्राह एवं तरन्तपुरुमीळ्हौ प्रतिजगृहतुः । तथा च शाट्यायनकम्--- ‘ अथ ह वै तरन्त पुरुमीळ्हौ वैददश्वी ध्वस्रयोः पुरुषन्त्योर्बहु प्रतिगृह्य गरगिराविव मेनाते तौ ह स्माङ्गुल्या सातं प्रतिममृशाते तावकामयेतामसातं नाविवेदं सातं स्यादात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतमिति तावेतञ्चतुर्ऋचमपश्यतां तेन प्रत्यैतां ततो वै तयोरसातं सातमभवदात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतं
evidence.gloss: Dhvasra is a certain king, Puruṣanti a certain other; of those two (the dual taken as a pair). ‘Thousands’: thousands of riches; ‘we accept’. The seer prays Soma that the wealth we accepted be excellent: so it is praise of Soma. As Avatsāra accepted these two’s riches, so did Taranta and Purumīḷha; and so the Śāṭyāyanaka: ‘Taranta and Purumīḷha, sons of Vidadaśva, having accepted much from Dhvasra and Puruṣanti, thought themselves like swallowers of poison; they touched the gain with a finger and wished: may this gain be no gain to us, as though merely taken, not accepted. They saw this four-verse hymn and by it went back; then their gain became no gain, as though merely taken, not accepted.’

reason: Second judgement with the refutation in hand. Re-ran day.js and verse.js (ok, Rig Veda 9.58.3, at [780,3]) and opened packet.js veda 96 for 9.58.1 to 9.58.4: on 9.58.3 Sāyaṇa glosses Dhvasra as a king (Puruṣanti ‘a certain one’, Wilson note 3 also two kings) and cites the Śāṭyāyanaka story of Taranta and Purumīḷha, garagirāv iva menāte, who saw this four-verse hymn (etaṃ caturṛcam apaśyatām) and their gain became as if not accepted; his 9.58.1 gloss names the subject as Soma. The refuter is right on both points, and both are correctable: (1) the plain sense ‘Its last two verses’ had no antecedent under a printed key verse and never named Soma, so it now reads ‘Closing a hymn to Soma, the singers turn to the gifts received’ (verses 3 and 4 close the four-verse hymn); (2) ‘uneasy at so much’ softened the Brāhmaṇa’s image, so it now reads ‘feeling like swallowers of poison’, the plain gloss of garagirāv iva menāte, instead of the refuter’s ‘dreading such wealth like poison’, which adds a dread the words do not carry. Reading, src and evidence unchanged; evidence confirmed as a contiguous verbatim span of the packet (74 words). entry-check ok at 44 words.
